en.summary: A Teochew-style bak kut teh restaurant on New Bridge Road. Peppery clear soup, pork ribs, braised sides and tea make a simple meal. A good food stop between the Singapore River and Chinatown. This card covers only the listed branch at No. 11.
en.fun_fact: Michelin notes the brand began as a pushcart on Johor Road in the late 1960s and is now run by the second generation. The pepper soup is refillable, a detail many diners remember.
en.hours: Daily hours not yet confirmed. Check the shop's or stall's notice on the day; it may sell out early.
en.price: $; hawker/home-style prices. Check the stall menu for actual prices.
en.access_notes: Michelin lists postal code 059386; a restaurant review site lists 059383. Navigate to 11 New Bridge Road and this card's verified coordinates first; the postal code needs confirming with the shop.
en.review_summary: One diner was unsure about white pepper soup beforehand, but after eating liked the soup and the tender ribs. (Small sample of visible reviews; not a consensus of all diners.)

en.summary: A long-running shop for Nyonya rice dumplings and kueh on East Coast Road, with a Peranakan culture visitor centre showing beaded shoes, clothing and family food traditions. A good start for a Katong–Joo Chiat walk: buy a few kueh, then stroll the shophouse streets.
en.fun_fact: The National Heritage Board records that founder Lee Kim Choo set up a stall in 1945 under a banyan tree where Joo Chiat Place meets Everitt Road. The family business grew from that stall and now also offers cultural talks.
en.hours: Check the official website for shop and visitor centre hours. Group tours need booking.
en.price: $; kueh sold individually. Ask about tours and workshops separately.
en.access_notes: Walk in for regular purchases. Contact them in advance for tours, beading or kueh-making sessions. Don't confuse Kim Choo Kueh Chang with similarly named brands.
en.coordinates_note: Named OpenStreetMap point for Kim Choo Kueh Chang, near East Coast Road and i12 Katong. This card is the 111 East Coast Road branch, not 62 Joo Chiat Place.
en.review_summary: One diner lists Nyonya rice dumplings, ondeh-ondeh, prawn glutinous rice rolls and otak-otak as what they come to buy. The review sample focuses on kueh choices. (Small sample of visible reviews; not a consensus of all diners.)

en.summary: A traditional coffee shop in a blue corner shophouse on East Coast Road, serving a Hainanese-style breakfast of kaya toast on round buns, soft-boiled eggs, kopi and pastries. Easy to pair with Holy Family Church in Katong, Joo Chiat shophouses and Peranakan culture stops.
en.fun_fact: The official website says the brand was founded in 1925 and describes the morning routine of slow-cooking kaya each day. Its signature is the sliced round bun, which looks different from the usual square toast.
en.hours: East Coast outlet: daily 08:00–16:00, last order 15:30. Check the official website for notices on the day.
en.price: $–$$; coffee, breakfast and pastries
en.access_notes: This card is the original East Coast shop. The official website also lists a NEX branch, so navigate by street address. Allow time to queue at weekends.
en.coordinates_note: Named point on public maps; the address 204 East Coast Road matches this card. Not the newer NEX branch.
en.review_summary: In August 2024 a diner liked the kaya buns and milk tea, noting a queue before 10am on a weekday but a short wait. They also said they personally prefer another toast shop. (Small sample of visible reviews; not a consensus of all diners.)

en.summary: A Malay steamed rice cake stall at Haig Road hawker centre. Rice flour is filled with gula melaka, steamed, and served with lightly salted grated coconut. A snack stop between Geylang Serai Market, Malay clothing shops and a Joo Chiat route.
en.fun_fact: The brand's website says it has operated since 1985. This Haig Road stall sells only the classic gula melaka flavour. The Singapore Tourism Board also notes the brand appeared on Netflix's Street Food Asia.
en.hours: Tue–Sun 10:45–21:30; usually closed Mon; public holidays 10:45–21:30. The day-of-week text on the official page is ambiguous, so confirm before going on a Monday.
en.price: $; sold per portion
en.access_notes: Uses the 14 Haig Road stall, which the official website clearly marks as open. Don't use the old 970 Geylang Road details still shown in the page footer. This stall takes walk-in purchases only.
en.coordinates_note: Named point on public maps; the address 14 Haig Road #01-07 matches this card and the business's website. Possibly outdated opening hours on the map are not used.
en.review_summary: In August 2024 a Burpple diner found the rice flour and gula melaka fragrant, a good dessert after a meal. In 2021 another diner especially liked the moist grated coconut. (Small sample of visible reviews; not a consensus of all diners.)

en.summary: The main Jalan Tampang shop for white bee hoon: thin rice vermicelli coated in seafood broth, alongside local zi char dishes. Fits a Sembawang history and northern neighbourhood route, combined with naval base sites, old shops and parks.
en.fun_fact: The brand says founder Tay King Huak started at a Chong Pang hawker stall in 1999 and moved to Jalan Tampang in 2000 after the market closed. A plate of bee hoon keeps a memory of the community's relocation.
en.hours: Daily 11:00–22:00, last order 21:30. Reservations accepted Mon–Fri.
en.price: $$; white bee hoon and shared zi char
en.access_notes: You still need to walk or take a connecting ride from the MRT station. This card is the Jalan Tampang main shop. The official website lists the Sun Plaza branch as permanently closed; don't mix them up.
en.coordinates_note: The official address 22 Jalan Tampang 758966 has been checked, but this branch's coordinates could not be found on public pages this time. The website embeds a Google My Maps of all outlets. Left as null rather than mixing in other branches or mall locations.
en.review_summary: Visible reviews for this address like the white bee hoon's seafood flavour and lime aroma, and also rate the salted egg prawns and chicken wings. Treat reviews of mall branches separately. (Small sample of visible reviews; not a consensus of all diners.)

en.summary: A long-running night-time nasi lemak shop on Sembawang Road. Choose chicken wings, fish, vegetables and sambal to go with your rice. It is Chinese-run nasi lemak, suited to a northern dinner or supper route, and should not be assumed halal.
en.fun_fact: The National Heritage Board links this shop to the old Chong Pang Village: the shop is named after the village, which was named after Lim Chong Pang, son of Lim Nee Soon. A night-time eatery keeps a trace of old village life.
en.hours: Reports list daily 17:00–06:00 the next day. Recheck night opening hours before you go.
en.price: $; priced by side dishes
en.access_notes: From the MRT station you need a bus or a long walk. Check night transport and last bus times separately.
en.coordinates_note: Named place on public maps, near Chong Pang Camp and Yishun Secondary School. Not a stall inside Chong Pang Market.
en.review_summary: Visible Tripadvisor reviewers especially praise the nasi lemak with fried chicken wings. Not enough recent individual reviews were found this time, so this is not an overall verdict. (Small sample of visible reviews; not a consensus of all diners.)

en.summary: A mangrove and migratory bird site reached by bus from Kranji. It helps you see Singapore as a wetland on a migration route, not just a garden city. Boardwalks, mudflats and bird hides let you watch wildlife up close, but sightings are not guaranteed.
en.fun_fact: It was Singapore's first ASEAN Heritage Park. The reserve covers 202 hectares, and officials note that high tides or bad weather may close some routes temporarily.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: From Kranji MRT take bus 925 (Mon–Sat) or 925M (Sun and public holidays). No cycling, jogging or pets. Plan around official tide and route closure notices.
en.review_summary: Visible visitor reviews mention seeing crocodiles, monitor lizards and many birds in about three hours. Some felt the loop near the Wetland Centre was more rewarding than the coastal stretch by the Visitor Centre. This is one person's day; you may not see the same animals.

en.summary: Mainly freshwater marsh, grassland and bird hides, for people who want quiet birdwatching away from the city. Climb the Raptor Tower to see the scale of the wetland by the reservoir. The public area is much smaller than the whole site; stick to the open trails.
en.fun_fact: The site covers 56.8 hectares, but only about 8 hectares are open to the public. The 15-metre Raptor Tower is about a 15-minute walk from the entrance. The core conservation area is open only for approved activities.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Needs a bus connection or taxi; it is not right outside an MRT exit. You can't enter the core area on your own. The tower has stairs only. No pets or cycling.
en.review_summary: Visitors in 2018 liked the small crowds, the bird tower and the open wetland. They also warned that unshaded stretches are hot, and some suggested combining it with nearby places. Reviews are older; use for a sense of the experience only.

en.summary: A small public hot spring space in the north. On normal days you can soak your feet, collect spring water and learn about local plants. It is not like a big hot spring resort, and suits people who value everyday local life. You can't visit during the current repairs.
en.fun_fact: Spring water flows from the top of a stepped foot-bath pool and cools as it passes through four tiers. There is also a water-collection and egg-cooking area at about 70°C. When open, visitors can bring their own eggs and containers to try this local habit.
en.hours: Currently closed until 2026-10-30; usually 07:00–19:00
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: As of 2026-10-29, official notices say the whole park is closed for urgent repairs until 30 October; check again after it reopens. No on-site car park; official guidance is to park at 114 Yishun Ring Road and walk.
en.review_summary: In August 2025 one visitor found the walk from Canberra long and the foot-bath area hot on sunny days, but thought it a fun "hot spring experience rare in Singapore". A 2024 visitor also enjoyed chatting with local regulars.

en.summary: A seafront promenade facing the Strait of Johor, where you can see how Singapore and Johor face each other across the water. Link the long jetty, playground and Admiralty Park into a northern walk. It feels more like an everyday residents' park.
en.fun_fact: The park's jetty is 400 metres long. NParks describes it as the northernmost point of mainland Singapore, with views across the Strait of Johor.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Reachable from Woodlands North. The park is wheelchair accessible. Fish only in designated areas; don't feed the monkeys.
en.review_summary: Visible visitor reviews like the open sea view towards Johor. Others clearly prefer the forest and mangroves of neighbouring Admiralty Park, so choose by whether you want sea views or nature.

en.summary: A large HDB-estate park that combines children's play with a nature area. One part suits slides, sports and family activities; another has secondary forest, a river and mangroves. Combine with Woodlands Waterfront Park for a half-day northern route.
en.fun_fact: The park has 26 slides. Officials say its nature area includes forest, mangrove, riverbank and grassland habitats, showing that varied ecology can survive in an ordinary neighbourhood.
en.hours: Park 24 hours; nature area 07:00–19:00
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Unpaved paths in the nature area are not suitable for wheelchairs. Families should follow on-site age and slide rules.
en.review_summary: In 2019 family visitors said there were many kinds of slides and kids were absorbed, but warned slides get hot in the sun, so come early and bring water. A 2023 review saw the nature area as a relaxing midday walk.

en.summary: A small waterfront park with views of the Strait of Johor, designated fishing areas and war memorial information. Good for a short stop before or after Sungei Buloh. The focus is border water views and history, not long hikes.
en.fun_fact: A war memorial plaque in the park records the 1942 Battle of Kranji Beach, linking this calm-looking shore to Singapore's wartime defence history.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Fish only in the designated Fishing Ground A/B. Don't climb over fences or fly drones.
en.review_summary: Personal reviews of the Area A fishing spot range from brief satisfaction to warnings about ants, mosquitoes and not always catching fish. These views cover only the fishing spot, not walking in the park as a whole.

en.summary: Forest trails pass the remains of an old Hainanese village. Surviving walls, floor tiles and information boards turn a hike into a walk through rural life history. Take it slowly to trace the links between homes, farmland and regrown forest; it is not just a ruins photo spot.
en.fun_fact: Hainanese and other migrant villages stood here from the 1930s to the 1980s. It is also an important site for conserving the critically endangered Raffles' banded langur.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Official directions put the main entrance about 2.3 km from Lentor. Only the entrance node is wheelchair accessible. No pets, cycling or leaving the marked trails.
en.review_summary: A 2022 visitor said the woods, small streams and village ruins were great for a short dose of nature. A 2023 review liked the scenery but felt nervous meeting monkeys and other wildlife. This is a personal feeling, not a risk rating.

en.summary: A lawn and beach park facing the Strait of Johor. Along the shore, the old jetty and nearby black-and-white houses help explain Sembawang's naval base past. It feels more like a neighbourhood hangout than city-centre waterfronts, and pairs well with heritage trails and northern food.
en.fun_fact: The British began building the 30-metre jetty in the early 1940s; it was completed during the Japanese Occupation. The name Sembawang also comes from the Sembawang tree, which you can see in the park.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: You still need a connecting ride after the MRT. The beach and jetty open depending on conditions on site. Official info lists car parks A/B as free.
en.review_summary: A 2024 visitor found it small and quiet, with historic buildings and a fishing jetty, but remote, and the shipyard view is not for everyone. 2023 reviews disagree on how clean the beach is.

en.summary: A neighbourhood water park right next to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital. See how green space beside a hospital serves walking, resting and bird habitats. Floating wetlands and a loop around the pond make it part of everyday life for Yishun residents.
en.fun_fact: The 14.5-metre spiral lookout tower is inspired by the butterfly life cycle and shaped like a cocoon. A bridge next to the tower leads to Yishun Park.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Park at the nearby hospital, Tzu Chi Humanistic Youth Centre or sports centre car parks. The park is wheelchair accessible; check on site for tower access.
en.review_summary: Visible personal reviews like the quiet pond-side mornings and sunrises. One runner uses the roughly 1 km loop to measure distance, and describes seeing birds, turtles and monitor lizards. The excerpts read showed no dates, and wildlife sightings are not guaranteed.

en.summary: A northern park known for waterside jogging, resting and water sports. A kelong-style bridge, rain gardens and open water make it a good stop on a water-and-everyday-life route around Khatib.
en.fun_fact: The Heritage Bridge imitates a traditional offshore kelong platform. The park's bioretention rain garden filters water naturally and helps ease flooding.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Water activities follow the operator's arrangements; fishing in designated areas only. Officials list the park as wheelchair accessible.
en.review_summary: Visitor reviews found describe it as a running, fishing and photography spot with relatively few tourists; another headline simply stresses calm and peace. This is a limited sample of reviews; no overall rating is inferred.

en.summary: Wide water, a simple lookout tower and shoreline trees make a quiet northern reservoir view, good for sunsets, photos and short walks. It is part of the Central Catchment protected area, with a very different pace from attraction-packed Marina Bay.
en.fun_fact: The 18-metre rocket-shaped lookout tower was built in 1969. The reservoir was first built in 1920 and listed as a historic site in 1999.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Needs a connecting ride after the MRT. No pets; watch out for monkeys and stay on marked paths.
en.review_summary: A 2019 visitor treated this as a regular place to unwind and liked the evening sun on the water. The review is older; use it for atmosphere, and check the official website for facilities and opening.

en.summary: A small freshwater wetland inside Seletar Aerospace Park. One loop around the boardwalk and water's edge lets you see birds and plants. Pair it with the black-and-white houses at The Oval and the aerospace park's public spaces rather than giving it most of a day.
en.fun_fact: It is only 3.23 hectares, but has been kept as a freshwater habitat. Officials note that waterbirds use its undisturbed setting to nest and rest.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: No car park in the park. No wheelchair link between the nature trail and boardwalk. No cycling on the boardwalk; no feeding fish, swimming or fishing.
en.review_summary: A 2020 visitor found the park small, with the core loop done in about 15 minutes, and liked going on to see the black-and-white houses at The Oval. A review published in 2025 mentions birdwatching and photography.

en.summary: A small riverside nature park near Springleaf MRT station, good for a walk along the waterway after eating at nearby local spots. It is also part of the Central Nature Park network, linking daily walking and cycling with a larger ecological buffer.
en.fun_fact: Officials have recorded more than 80 resident and migratory bird species here. After nearby villages and plantations were abandoned, some fig and sterculia trees kept growing naturally.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Official walking directions from Springleaf MRT are about 550 m. The park is wheelchair accessible. No fishing or leaving marked trails.
en.review_summary: Visible visitor reviews found the park small but calm, and mention convenient water points and toilets. They also warn unshaded areas are hot; you can keep walking along the river towards Lower Seletar Reservoir.

en.summary: An island park reached by bridge. Sandy paths, casuarina woods, mangroves and small beaches feel different from city parks. Combine with Punggol coast and Lorong Halus, but services on the island are limited, so allow time to get in and out.
en.fun_fact: The park has five beaches, each themed around different plants. Near Area C are the only two wild Paku Raja cycads on mainland Singapore; they grow extremely slowly.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: West Gate is near Punggol Point; East Gate is near Lorong Halus. Wear closed shoes and long trousers against sandflies. Some ground is uneven. Haw Par Beach Villa is off-limits.
en.review_summary: Visitors in 2020–2021 liked cycling, the nature trails and small beaches. Some advised checking the entrance in advance and noted few supplies on the island; others met monkeys snatching food. These are past experiences; follow NParks for access rules.

en.summary: A public waterway running through Punggol New Town, linking HDB blocks, malls, activity facilities and waterside leisure. See how a new town organises life around water. Pick one section to suit your time; no need to walk the whole waterway.
en.fun_fact: About 160 metres of old Punggol Road and an old bus stop were kept when the park was built. Kelong Bridge is shaped like a fishing village kelong, remembering Punggol's fishing past.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Wheelchair accessible and suitable for seniors. Pedestrians share paths with cyclists, so stay alert. No fishing. At night, keep to well-lit sections where possible.
en.review_summary: Reviews say the paths are gentle and the water views suit running, walking, sunrise and sunset; some warn of many bicycles. In 2023 one visitor felt it is better visited on the way than worth a special trip across the island.

en.summary: A riverside park next to Sengkang HDB estates. Constructed wetlands, fruit trees and trails give a real-life view of water planning. Enter different zones from LRT stations, and combine a river walk with nearby hawker centres and sports facilities for an everyday residents' route.
en.fun_fact: It has one of Singapore's larger constructed wetlands. A 290-metre riverside bridge links the two banks, and a fruit-themed boardwalk echoes the park's twenty-plus kinds of fruit trees.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: About a 5-minute walk from Kupang or Farmway LRT to the respective zones. The pond area is not wheelchair accessible. No fishing.
en.review_summary: A 2019 runner rated the track but complained someone was playing loud music near the café at the time. A 2020 visitor enjoyed spotting animals in the park. Small, older sample; not representative of the atmosphere all day.

en.summary: An eco green space surrounded by roads and housing, with grassland, woodland, wetland and more natural paths. Look for weaver bird nests, butterflies and waterbirds, and experience habitat inside the city that is kept less neatly trimmed.
en.fun_fact: The park's eco-toilets use bacteria and wood shavings to treat waste, with no water or chemicals. Standing dead trees are kept on purpose, not from neglect: birds use them for food and nesting.
en.hours: 24 hours, but no lighting at night; officials suggest leaving before 19:00
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: No cycling, pets or fishing. Wheelchairs can use only the paved outer path; the inner dirt trails are unsuitable.
en.review_summary: A 2020 visitor found it quiet inside despite roads on all sides, with easy paths and many butterflies. A 2019 review liked the birds, marsh and short loop. Very few reviews.

en.summary: Seaside leisure, large mature trees and a mangrove boardwalk in one park, good for both family activities and nature watching. Split your route into a coastal walk and a mangrove section; the bird tower and kitchen garden are also worth a stop.
en.fun_fact: The park has about 6 hectares of mangroves, which you can view from the boardwalk and bird tower. The kitchen garden shows visitors edible and everyday-use plants.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: The coast and intertidal zone are fragile; don't touch or collect wildlife. Follow on-site notices about sea water and wildlife.
en.review_summary: In April 2026 a visitor liked the trail from the river to the sea, the mature trees and birds. In 2024 a resident who runs here often complained about litter on the beach. Experiences vary by area and maintenance timing.

en.summary: An old seaside park near Changi Village and the Pulau Ubin ferry terminal. Watch the sea, walk, cycle and see planes. Taken together, the beach, ferries and wartime memorial information show the layered history of the east coast.
en.fun_fact: A WWII memorial plaque in the park describes the 1942 Changi Beach massacre. Memory of the Sook Ching history is kept within a leisure landscape; take time to read the information.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: After the MRT, take a bus to Changi Village. No camping or tents. Wear closed shoes on the intertidal zone; don't step on or collect wildlife.
en.review_summary: Visible reviews from October 2024 liked the quiet coast and sunsets. These are personal impressions from the reviews seen; judge beach cleanliness and tides on the day.

en.summary: A long coastal park linking cycling, barbecues, family activities and hawker food. It is worth saving by entrance and area: one card can stand for the main coastline, while actual routes pick sections by destination and open paths.
en.fun_fact: Officials list the park at 180 hectares, stretching more than 13 km along the coast. KPMG Wellness Garden is the east's first multi-generational garden for people of different ages and abilities.
en.hours: Park 24 hours; some beaches, paths and facilities temporarily closed
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: As of 2026-10-29, the Area D beach is closed for oil spill clean-up, and there are works in Area D and on the C1/C4 paths. Check NParks notices before you go; routes must not pass through closed areas.
en.review_summary: A 2026 visitor liked the flat cycling paths and children's facilities, but warned it is crowded at weekends. A 2024 visitor complained about noise and litter and preferred weekday mornings.

en.summary: A park around a reservoir, very close to the MRT station. Watch how running, water sports, bird-keeping and community leisure share the same water. Walk just the floating platform and songbird area, or go all the way around the reservoir.
en.fun_fact: The park was converted from an old sand quarry. Besides the 4.3 km gravel loop, on weekend mornings the songbird area shows the local bird-keeping culture of hanging cages on tall poles.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Official directions say about a 200 m walk from Bedok Reservoir MRT. Water sports and high-element activities are booked and charged separately.
en.review_summary: In October 2025 a nearby resident said the 4.3 km loop is a good length for running and walking, and liked the water sports and nearby food options. A personal recommendation.

en.summary: A nature park known for regenerating secondary forest, understorey plants and streams. Good for short boardwalk walks, and also a gateway to longer catchment hikes. When planning, keep the easy loops in the park separate from the long route to the TreeTop Walk.
en.fun_fact: Drongo Trail is named after the greater racket-tailed drongo, a glossy black bird with two very long tail feathers ending in rackets. The trail name doubles as a birdwatching hint.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: About 1.1–1.2 km walk from Upper Thomson or Bright Hill. No pets or cycling. The car park can't be entered or exited after 19:00; no overnight parking.
en.review_summary: An April 2026 visitor said the forest is richly layered and you can choose routes to suit your fitness; not difficult overall, but bring mosquito protection. A 2020 review especially liked the quiet forest path of Venus Loop.

en.summary: A naturalised river and wide lawns run through the neighbourhood, a key example of Singapore's water management and public space design. Watch residents run and walk dogs, and compare the winding river and cleansing plants with the dense housing around them.
en.fun_fact: The Kallang River was once confined to a concrete channel along the park's southern edge; it was later turned into a naturalised river. The Cleansing Biotope uses plants to help keep water clean in the ponds and water features.
en.hours: Open 24 hours; some bridges and entrances under works
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: As of 2026-10-29, the bridge near Bishan Park Condominium has works until end-December, and the bridge near Dragonfly Pond until 4 December. Some entrances are closed for LTA works; use alternative bridges.
en.review_summary: Family visitors in 2025 liked the wide space, the naturalised river and activities for children and pets. Another 2025 visitor felt the designed landscape still feels natural. A sample of visible reviews.

en.summary: A nature park where an old quarry has become wetland and forest trails. Visit alongside the Beauty World neighbourhood and the Rail Corridor. Boardwalks, a bird hide and high viewpoints show how mined land has turned into new habitat.
en.fun_fact: Today's Quarry Wetland comes from the old Sin Seng Quarry. The nest-like Waterhen Hide lets visitors watch the wetland while disturbing animals less.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: There is an accessible route of about 700 m from the visitor pavilion to Quarry Wetland; assess other climbs and dirt trails separately. No pets, fishing or cycling.
en.review_summary: The only visible review (visit in July 2025, posted in October) says it is reachable from Beauty World, trails and signs are clear, and visitor facilities are good. One review only; not an overall verdict.

en.summary: One of the reserves where Singapore still keeps primary tropical rainforest. The summit route lets you feel steep slopes, buttress roots and dense forest next to the city. Good for serious forest watching. Routes may not be long, but don't assume they're easy just because the hill is low.
en.fun_fact: Bukit Timah Hill is about 163 m, Singapore's highest natural point. The reserve has a Seraya tree about 60 m tall, roughly the height of a twenty-storey HDB block.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Slopes and steps are steep. Wheelchair access covers only the gallery and the area near the toilets. No pets. Hikers and mountain bikers use separate designated routes.
en.review_summary: Visible visitors like the rainforest preserved next to the city. In 2020 an older hiker described the Dairy Farm route up as tiring with continuous high steps, and the way down hard on the knees. A personal fitness experience.

en.summary: A woodland park on a former dairy farm, combining the Wallace Education Centre, a quarry and hiking trails. See how food production, mining and ecological recovery overlap. If you choose an easy route, don't accidentally join the steep Bukit Timah summit trail.
en.fun_fact: There are two kinds of quarry remains here: Dairy Farm Quarry was filled in as land, while Singapore Quarry became a lake. The education centre is named after naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace.
en.hours: Park 07:00–19:00; education centre 08:30–17:00, closed Mon; Singapore Quarry 08:00–18:30
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Wheelchair access from Carpark B to the education centre. No pets on Wallace Trail; only leashed pets from Carpark A to Singapore Quarry.
en.review_summary: An April 2025 visitor liked the green space linking to Rifle Range and the gentler forest paths, finding it an easy way into nature. Follow the current park map for specific routes.

en.summary: An easier nature park next to Bukit Timah Nature Reserve. Highlights are the steep quarry walls and reflections on still water. Good if you want landscapes and trees without climbing to the summit; pair with Beauty World food for a short route.
en.fun_fact: The quarry is now a lake view and wildlife habitat. Officials say you can reach the accessible route via the ramp in front of the Bukit Timah visitor centre.
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: No pets. An old 2025 boardwalk repair notice expected completion in January 2026; still check the latest entrances and on-site notices before going.
en.review_summary: A 2021 visitor said it is fairly flat once you reach the lake and the quarry view is good, but it is very hot in the afternoon. They saw monkeys and monitor lizards but no birds that day, showing wildlife sightings are a matter of chance.

en.summary: A woodland park centred on an old quarry. Besides the water and rock face, an uphill route leads to a war memorial site. Choose between the easy lakeside walk and the harder heritage trail; don't treat the two as one effortless route.
en.fun_fact: The park was developed on an abandoned quarry in 1988. A WWII memorial plaque around Lorong Sesuai makes this nature spot a war history site too.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: The lakeside and uphill routes need different fitness levels. Pets must be leashed; no fishing.
en.review_summary: A 2025 visitor found it pleasant for a short walk of an hour or two. A 2021 hiker warned the slope to the war memorial is steep, and enjoyed the variety of birds and insects along the way.

en.summary: A rock-face lake view near HDB blocks and the MRT station, best for a short stop to photograph reflections and see old quarry terrain. It is a different place from Bukit Batok Nature Park; save them separately, then decide whether to link them.
en.fun_fact: The abandoned quarry filled with water to form a lake in the 1980s. The mix of rock face and water reminded people of Guilin, earning it the nickname Little Guilin.
en.hours: Open 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: No dedicated car park. Officials list it as accessible. No pets or fishing.
en.review_summary: An April 2025 visitor was surprised how photogenic it is and how close to the MRT, but felt it suits residents exploring on the way. A 2023 review liked the calm water view and advised mosquito protection.

en.summary: A public garden built around learning about gardening. Themed gardens, edible plants and pollinator displays reward slow looking, not just passing through on the Southern Ridges. Good for families, plant lovers and anyone studying urban greenery.
en.fun_fact: The park has more than ten themed gardens. The bee trail has "bee hotels" that show how different bee species live; officials ask visitors not to touch them.
en.hours: 06:00–23:00; visitor services hours listed separately
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Some gardens get strong sun. Combine with Alexandra Arch and Telok Blangah routes. Don't touch the bee hotels.
en.review_summary: A 2021 family visitor liked being able to identify plants such as cotton, bananas and vegetables. Another review that year found the gardens pretty, but lacking shade, with a steep uphill at the back gate.

en.summary: Hilltop terrace gardens, an elevated forest walk and Henderson Waves form a multi-level walking space above the Telok Blangah housing estate. See high-rises, the port and the tree canopy side by side. You can extend to Mount Faber or HortPark.
en.fun_fact: Henderson Waves is 274 m long and Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge. Its undulating timber ribs are both a design feature and alcoves for sitting, so crossing the bridge becomes a viewing experience in itself.
en.hours: Park 24 hours; don't enter Earth Trail after 19:00
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Many slopes and stairs; officials mark it as not wheelchair friendly. The park being open at night doesn't mean every forest path is safe to walk at night.
en.review_summary: Visitors found say the park is well kept and pleasant to walk, and include breakfast at the HDB blocks below as part of the trip. Another visitor liked taking photos in the gardens. Based on a small sample.

en.summary: Enter Marang Trail near HarbourFront MRT and climb steps up the ridge to views of the port, Sentosa and the southern islands. The park links a city transport hub with forest, a good way to understand southern Singapore's hills and sea on foot.
en.fun_fact: Marang Trail is only about 700 m, but its continuous steps connect the Telok Blangah Road area straight up to the ridge. The sharp height gain over a short distance means one walk takes in streets, forest and high sea views.
en.hours: 24 hours
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Marang Trail is steep with stairs. The commercial cable car and dining at the top cost extra. Adjust walking time to your fitness.
en.review_summary: Visitors especially recommend the all-round views and shade at Faber Point; others like the quiet forest trail. Reviews distinguish the cable car station from the actual viewpoint, a hint not to stop only at the commercial area.

en.summary: This links coastal secondary forest, a rocky shore and old coastal defence remains. Enter by the mangrove boardwalk near the MRT station, then join the seaside park and Keppel Coastal Trail to see how a waterfront city keeps small pockets of natural habitat.
en.fun_fact: The Dragon's Teeth Gate in the park is a commemorative replica. The original rock landmark was blown up in 1848 to widen the shipping channel. This old-looking seaside symbol actually tells how port development changed the land.
en.hours: Park 24 hours; nature reserve section 07:00–19:00
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Some coastal boardwalks are wheelchair accessible. Pets allowed only in the park and permitted boardwalks, not in the reserve. No cycling or drones.
en.review_summary: Visitors like starting from the MRT and linking the coastal boardwalk with the harbour walk; they also note little shade on the seaside stretch. Older reviews say the forest section is cool and you can see old coastal defence structures as you walk. Review dates have been kept.

en.summary: Lakeside boardwalks, forest dirt trails and kayaking make up a classic local outdoor routine. A short route can stay by the water; a long one goes into the Central Catchment. Good for understanding water supply history, tropical forest and popular sport on one route.
en.fun_fact: MacRitchie is Singapore's oldest reservoir. PUB added walkways close to the water along the edge, so a body of water built for supply is also a space where people can get close to the water.
en.hours: Reserve and forest trails 07:00–19:00; TreeTop Walk has separate opening times
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: This card uses the southern reservoir park as the entrance. The TreeTop Walk is far from the entrance and not part of a short route. Main park spaces are wheelchair accessible; not all forest trails are. Don't feed the monkeys. Coordinates use the historic marker at the foot of Hilltop in the southern park, from third-party citations of NHB geodata; marked approximate. On site, enter from the park entrance on Reservoir Road.
en.review_summary: Visitors like the lakeside vegetation and the small wildlife you may meet, but some long-distance hikers found it hot, humid and tiring. Seeing animals is a matter of chance; another visitor came specially for monkeys and saw none.

en.summary: Lakeside Garden, Chinese Garden and Japanese Garden make up a national garden of about 90 hectares. Lakeside paths, grassland bird habitats, children's nature play and Asian gardens share one area. Split it into several short visits instead of rushing everything at once.
en.fun_fact: The Lone Tree on the grassland, often photographed as a dead tree, is actually made from steel bars recycled from old park paths. It nods to Jurong's industrial history and gives birds of prey an open perch.
en.hours: Lakeside Garden 24 hours; Chinese Garden and Japanese Garden 05:30–24:00; special facilities separate
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Coordinates are for the official management office, Gardenhouse, not the entrance nearest Lakeside MRT. Toilets at Waterwall Court and Sunken Garden are under repair. The shuttle is suspended on 2026-10-29, 10-30 and 11-03. Nature areas such as Grasslands have no night lighting.
en.review_summary: Visitors like the scale of the gardens and details to explore slowly, such as bonsai and waterfalls, and see it as an everyday place for residents to relax. Older reviews mention garden works; this has been updated with 2026 official opening information.

en.summary: Take a bumboat from Changi Point to an island that still has village houses, fruit trees, granite quarries and cycling roads. A slow walk around the village, the Sensory Trail and quarry views suit half a day. If extending to Chek Jawa, allow separate time for transport and walking.
en.fun_fact: Pulau Ubin was originally five small islands separated by tidal rivers. Bunds were later built for prawn farming, gradually joining them into today's single island. Its landscape has a natural granite base and also shows how production reshaped the environment.
en.hours: Island information kiosk daily 09:00–17:00; bumboats generally run on demand 06:00–19:00
en.price: Public trails on the island are free. Bumboat usually S$4 per person one way, plus S$2 for your own bicycle. Bike rental and food extra.
en.access_notes: The MRT listed is the transfer station for Changi Village, not a walking stop on the island. Bumboats usually leave once 12 people are on board. Chartering with fewer people or evening trips must be negotiated. Leave spare time for the return. Some Chek Jawa boardwalks are closed; see that card. Coordinates are the island's public jetty arrival point, not the geometric centre of the island.
en.review_summary: Visitors describe forgetting the city's busyness for a while as they cycle through villages, forest, beaches and mangroves. This is an actual review from the Pulau Ubin attraction listing; it doesn't represent all bike rental or tour operators.

en.summary: About 100 hectares of wetland at the eastern end of Pulau Ubin, where sandy beach, rocky shore, seagrass, coral rubble, mangroves and coastal forest meet. Boardwalks and Jejawi Tower give views from different heights. Tides strongly change which ecological details you can see.
en.fun_fact: It was once slated for reclamation. As the public came to know its ecological value in 2000, public attention and expert consultation led to the 2001 announcement deferring reclamation. Chek Jawa is a key place to understand civic participation in Singapore conservation.
en.hours: Wetlands daily 07:00–19:00; check local repair notices before going
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Part of the Coastal Loop boardwalk has been closed since 2026-09-15, with repairs expected until 2027-04-30. Mangrove Loop and unaffected parts remain open. Guided wetland tours are suspended for floating pontoon repairs. Don't go down onto the shore based on photos. Bicycles must be parked in designated areas. Coordinates are the visitor centre reference point, not the intertidal entry point.
en.review_summary: Visitors like the boardwalk over the water and the view from the tower; a family review said animals along the way gave plenty to talk about. One person visited at high tide and saw no small underwater creatures. Reviews predate the current repairs, so don't assume the whole route is open now.

en.summary: Take a boat from Marina South Pier to a marine park focused on coral reefs and marine conservation. Public visits are on Big Sister's Island, where coastal forest trails and a floating boardwalk let you see the island shore, very different from the city's man-made waterfronts.
en.fun_fact: The floating boardwalk is not just for walking; it also serves as coral habitat and for research. The marine park also includes reefs around Small Sister's Island and nearby islands; the public area is only part of it.
en.hours: Big Sister's Island 07:00–19:00; closed on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of each month, except on designated public holidays
en.price: Public areas free. Return ferries and commercial tours charged separately at the operator's fares on the day.
en.access_notes: Small Sister's Island and other research and conservation areas are closed to the public. No camping, barbecues, fishing, cycling or taking shells. For groups of 20 or more, email marinepark@nparks.gov.sg at least two weeks ahead. Confirm return boat times in advance.
en.review_summary: A visitor who joined a low-tide guided walk describes seeing sea anemones, seagrass and sea stars, and liked the sunset on the way back. This review is older and about a specific tour; animal sightings and current activities are not guaranteed.

en.summary: Next to a former landfill, a water facility is presented as ponds, reed beds and trails. A red footbridge links the Punggol and Pasir Ris sides. Good for a walk that ties together urban waste, water protection and riverside leisure.
en.fun_fact: The wetland is not just a landscape pond: PUB uses it to collect and treat leachate from the old landfill, keeping untreated water out of Serangoon Reservoir. The natural-looking reeds and ponds are doing an infrastructure job.
en.hours: Official sources list no fixed closing time; visit in daytime and follow on-site notices
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: Riviera is an LRT station and Punggol is the MRT interchange gateway; neither is right at the wetland. There are many unshaded stretches. Allow enough distance when linking with Punggol Waterway or Coney Island. Operational notices and water facility fences take priority. Coordinates are a wetland reference point; on site, navigate by the wetland entrance and footbridge.
en.review_summary: Visitors find the red bridge good for photos and the trail educational about the environment; one walked about 20 minutes from Riviera to the bridge. Older reviews warn it is hot in the day; pair it with a slow riverside walk.

en.summary: The rooftop lawn is a public space for kite flying, picnics and skyline views; below it is engineering that holds water and controls flooding. A visit can go from rooftop views to the water story, so seeing the city also becomes a way into Singapore's water management.
en.fun_fact: The barrage opened officially in 2008, creating Singapore's 15th reservoir, and the first in the city centre, in Marina Channel. It handles water supply, flood control and leisure at once.
en.hours: Public areas and Green Roof 24 hours; Sustainable Singapore Gallery 09:00–18:00, closed 12:00–13:00 and on Tuesdays
en.price: Free entry; parking and independently run activities extra
en.access_notes: The water play area and indoor gallery have their own hours; don't assume them from the roof being open all day. The roof has ramps and lifts. Follow on-site arrangements during events or bad weather. Coordinates are a reference point at the barrage pump house; follow on-site signs for the public visitor entrance.
en.review_summary: Visitors generally see the skyline view from the lawn as the highlight; some felt there is little to see if you want packed attractions. Good for sitting, kite watching or engineering talks. Reviews warn that walking routes meet cyclists.

en.summary: At the URA Centre, city models, interactive displays and film explain land planning, infrastructure and building conservation. Good as a primer before a city walk; then go to Chinatown, Tanjong Pagar and HDB estates to see the spatial links shown in the model.
en.fun_fact: The large model has a projection show of about three minutes that uses light to overlay planning strategies on real landmarks. It turns abstract land use and transport plans into a city structure you can see from above.
en.hours: Mon–Sat 09:00–17:00; closed Sun and public holidays
en.price: Free
en.access_notes: Partially closed 2026-12-01 to 2027-04-30; fully closed from 2027-05-01, expected to reopen in Q4 2027. Groups over 20 must book. Lifts and accessible facilities available.
en.review_summary: Visitors especially like the large city model, finding it helps them understand how Singapore developed. One finished in about an hour and used it as an air-conditioned learning stop during a Chinatown walk.

en.summary: A public building next to the MRT that stacks seniors' housing, healthcare, food, a community plaza and gardens vertically. Come to see how daily life shares facilities, then linger in the plaza or hawker centre. Fits a city and community design theme.
en.fun_fact: WOHA describes the design as a layered "sandwich": the community plaza, medical centre, and park and housing above all nest together. The building was the backdrop for the Prime Minister's 2018 National Day Rally speech and won World Building of the Year at the World Architecture Festival.
en.hours: Public spaces and facilities have different hours; rooftop garden access to be confirmed on site
en.price: Public areas free; food and services extra
en.access_notes: This is a working community and seniors' housing complex. Enter only public spaces, not residential corridors or controlled medical or childcare areas. The management has not clearly confirmed rooftop opening hours, so routes should offer ground-level public areas as an alternative.
en.review_summary: Visible personal reviews find its links to the MRT, food and daily services convenient, good for a neighbourhood stroll on the way. Other visitors found it noisy and crowded during events and criticised the cleanliness of some public areas. Excerpt dates not shown.

en.summary: WOHA-designed public housing that puts community spaces on different floors and makes the roof a public park. Link it with Margaret Drive and a Queenstown neighbourhood walk to see how Singapore HDB flats keep shared outdoor space at high density.
en.fun_fact: The project has 960 flats but no enclosed internal common corridors. About every 80 flats share a naturally ventilated "sky village", and at the top is a walking loop of about 300 m, turning neighbourly links into spatial design.
en.hours: A visitor platform lists 07:00–22:00; not confirmed live by management, so follow on-site notices
en.price: Public community spaces free
en.access_notes: Enter only the public gardens. Lifts are shared with residents; keep your voice down and keep passages clear. Older reviews mentioned maintenance, so current rooftop access needs rechecking. Don't treat the project website's public design description as a promise of permanent all-day access.
en.review_summary: One visitor said the 47th-storey garden has views of the city centre, the harbour and Sentosa, and links to a nearby hawker centre; some maintenance was going on then but it was still reachable. Only one older review, so the reminder to check on site stays.

en.summary: Walk between old barracks buildings to visit commercial galleries and eateries, and see how art activity moves into conserved buildings. The courtyards are close together but each has its own pace. Combine with Labrador coast or the Southern Ridges, and choose a time when exhibitions are open.
en.fun_fact: The barracks were built in 1936 and named after British general Webb Gillman. After independence they were also used for Singapore Armed Forces training. Today's galleries, eateries and shady courtyards carry layers of military and urban reuse history.
en.hours: Each venue has its own hours; Sundaram Tagore Gallery Tue–Sat 11:00–19:00, closed on some public holidays
en.price: Public grounds free; galleries, exhibitions and food as set by each operator
en.access_notes: Coordinates are for the gallery at 5 Lock Road. Announcements in 2026 adjusted housing and green space plans; no live site-wide closure notice was found. Check current exhibition dates before visiting a specific gallery. Many galleries are closed on Mondays.
en.review_summary: Visitors note it is made up of several commercial galleries and suits people interested in contemporary art; you can't always tell what's showing before you go in. Another visitor praised the works and friendly staff. Don't think of it as a single museum.

en.summary: Black-and-white houses, lawns, aviation-themed play equipment and runway-side paths kept within an aerospace industrial park. Good for the theme of how an airport becomes a living space. It connects to Hampstead Wetlands Park, so architecture, plane watching and nature fit in one half-day.
en.fun_fact: About 32 colonial-era houses survive around The Oval, originally homes for Royal Air Force staff and families. During renewal, the restoration team kept the original pitched-roof tiles and sourced suitable green embossed door glass to continue the houses' details.
en.hours: No set hours listed for outdoor public spaces; restaurants and shops keep their own hours. Visit in daytime.
en.price: Public grounds free; food, activities and parking extra
en.access_notes: The MRT listed is a transfer gateway; you need a bus or car to connect. Watch planes only from public paths and viewing areas; airport and company facilities are not open to wander in. No unified evening hours obtained. Map coordinates come from the embedded map of the park's property agent.
en.review_summary: One visitor found lists the black-and-white houses, old trees, aviation history and the nearby wetland as most worth a slow walk. Only one older review; the restaurants and building interiors it mentions are not guaranteed open now.

en.summary: From the public areas of Jewel Changi Airport, watch the indoor waterfall and Forest Valley from different floors. Fit it into an arrival or departure day, or make it a stop on an eastern city architecture route. The waterfall doesn't run all day; if you want the evening light show, check show times first.
en.fun_fact: The Rain Vortex is about 40 m tall, billed officially as the world's tallest indoor waterfall, with water falling through seven storeys. The Forest Valley around it gathers retail, transport and tropical greenery in the airport complex around one visual centre.
en.hours: Rain Vortex daily 10:00–22:00. Light and sound show: Mon–Thu 20:00, 21:00; Fri–Sun, public holidays and eves have an extra 22:00 show.
en.price: Viewing the Rain Vortex is free; Canopy Park and other attractions are ticketed separately
en.access_notes: In the landside public area; the MRT station is in the terminal, so you walk into Jewel. Coordinates are a reference point for the whole Jewel building. Early flights may miss the waterfall starting at 10:00. Separately ticketed attractions have different hours.
en.review_summary: Visitors enjoy viewing the waterfall from different floors and especially recommend the evening lights. One early-flight traveller made a separate trip because the waterfall only starts at 10:00.

en.summary: A one-kilometre outdoor dinosaur display along an airport connector, turning a cycling and running path into a family photo route. Combine with East Coast cycling or a walk around the airport. It is still some distance from the MRT exit, so factor in connections and walking time.
en.fun_fact: The trail shows more than twenty life-size dinosaur models of nine species; the tallest is nearly five metres. It is not a ticketed theme park but a long-term outdoor display on an everyday park connector.
en.hours: Daily, 24 hours
en.price: Free
en.access_notes: From Hub & Spoke at Terminal 2, walk or cycle about 2 km along the connector; or take a shuttle to Terminal 4 first and walk. Map coordinates are a reference point on the display stretch, not the MRT entrance. The path is shared with bicycles, and some exhibits have protective netting in front.
en.review_summary: Actual visitors find it good as a stretch on a bike ride or for family photos. Others note the path is narrow and hot, the experience suffers when there are many cyclists and pedestrians, and the netting blocks some photos.

en.summary: A five-hectare park in Jurong Innovation District that places ceramic works, a butterfly garden, an eco-pond and shady paths among industrial estates. Link it with the nearby dragon kilns for a half-day pottery and nature route. A new walking and cycling bridge makes this former Jurong Eco-Garden easier for Jurong West residents to reach.
en.fun_fact: Formerly Jurong Eco-Garden, it reopened as The Potter's Garden on 16 November 2025. The new name nods to Singapore's last two traditional dragon kilns nearby, and works by local potters line the paths.
en.hours: The official page shows no set opening hours; visit in daytime and follow on-site access and works notices
en.price: Public park; no ticketing information found
en.access_notes: Older maps may still show Jurong Eco-Garden. Don't treat future Jurong Region Line stations as operating MRT stations. Boon Lay / Pioneer are transfer gateways; take a bus, then walk. Coordinates are a reference point for the original garden; to enter, navigate first to the connecting bridge near Block 864A.
en.review_summary: Visible personal reviews like the greenery, water features and space for casual running after the makeover, and suggest early morning or evening. Others warn some gravel paths may be uneven or slippery. The excerpts show no dates, so they can't confirm conditions on a given day.

en.summary: A farm in the Kranji countryside where you can see tropical food plants and combine a farm walk with on-site dining. Plan it as a dedicated stop in the northern countryside, allowing driving time if combining with wetlands or other farms. Check weekday opening and booking details before going.
en.fun_fact: The farm was founded in 2000 by Ivy Singh and her husband Lim Ho Seng, once under the name Bollywood Veggies. It combines growing, farm dining and education, showing another way of living with the land in a city-state.
en.hours: Official website table: Wed–Fri 10:00–15:00; Sat, Sun and public holidays 07:00–18:00. It also lists Mon–Thu for booked private events, so phone to confirm before a weekday visit.
en.price: Walk-in entry fee not clearly stated on official pages; food, workshops and private bookings extra
en.access_notes: The official website says there is no direct public transport; take a taxi or ride-hail from Kranji MRT. Free car park. The website's weekday hours overlap with its private event notice, so phone first, especially for Wed and Thu. Tours, workshops and private events must be booked.
en.review_summary: Older reviews like the rural atmosphere and walks before or after meals. Opinions differ on the food and booking service; weekend waits and busy parking are also mentioned. The reviews read are older and don't reflect current service.

en.summary: At the goat farm's current site, watch morning milking, then see and feed goats in the open pens. Combine with Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve for a northern nature-and-food route. It offers a close look at livestock farming. Come early to see milking; visitors don't milk the goats themselves.
en.fun_fact: This goat farm, running since 1988, makes daily milking part of the visit. Officials say the goats line up and walk to their own spots, and visitors can watch this daily routine from the viewing area.
en.hours: 09:00–16:00; closed Tue, except public holidays. Milking viewing 09:00–10:30; feed sold until 15:00.
en.price: Walk-in visitors free; alfalfa feed S$6 per pack; groups of 10 or more must book a paid educational tour
en.access_notes: The current site is 250 Neo Tiew Crescent; don't navigate to the old site at Lim Chu Kang Lane 4. Groups under 10 can walk in; 10 or more must book. The website asks that you haven't visited a cattle farm in the month before. Visitors can't milk the goats. Bus 925M serves the Wetland Centre only on Sundays and public holidays; on other days arrange a car. If driving, park at the Sungei Buloh Neo Tiew Crescent entrance car park, then cross the road and enter by the side gate; the farm has no visitor parking.
en.review_summary: In older reviews from the previous site, family visitors liked watching milking and feeding goats, and warned the pens smell strongly and you need to wash hands afterwards. Use these only as a guide to the type of experience; for transport and facilities at the current site, follow the new official information.

en.area: Seletar Club Road / Lower Seletar Reservoir
en.summary: A waterside stretch by Lower Seletar Reservoir where you can rest in a pavilion, watch the wetland from a boardwalk, and stop during a ride. It is very different from city-centre waterfronts, for people who want to see everyday northern shores and park connectors.
en.fun_fact: It is a stop on the first 60 km phase of the Round Island Route. Wetlands and vegetated swales combine rest space with rainwater management. The park also has native plants that give herons and other wildlife food and habitat.
en.hours: The official page shows no separate access hours; visit in daytime and follow on-site notices
en.price: Free
en.access_notes: Officials list the connector stretch at about 0.8 km, and it is wheelchair accessible. Take bus 103, 117 or 117M to Opp JTC Aviation Two, then walk; the MRT station is a transfer gateway. Check lighting and entrances before planning evening activities.
en.review_summary: The same visitor, in two reviews, describes it as a quiet waterside rest stop on a ride and likes the pavilion view and short boardwalk. A limited sample; not a broad consensus.
